cells.tense: You are standing in your own knowing right now, and you are acting from it — releasing what has finished and keeping what still feeds, without a committee in your head about it.
cells.ask: Offer one ending you have already chosen, spoken where it can be heard, so the ground stays clear for what you are growing.
cells.core:
When this is working, you read a room or a season and know what has to go and what has to stay, and you move on it quietly. The finished thing gets let go before it turns sour. What is still alive gets kept and fed. Nothing is wasted by you — what you set down is folded back into the ground of the next thing, so the next thing starts stronger than the last. People stand on what you have tended without noticing it was tended, and that is the whole craft.

What you have not done yet is say the ending out loud. Naming it costs almost nothing and clears the same ground twice — once for you, once for whoever was standing on it with you.
cells.sheetLine: You know what to release and what to keep, and you act on it.

cells.tense: You are bracing for something that has not arrived yet, clearing ground for a season you cannot see, and the clearing has stopped being about what is actually here.
cells.ask: Stay beside one person with whatever they are feeling today — no fixing, no planning their next step — and let that be the whole of what you do for them.
cells.core:
When this is working, your sense of what has to end comes from what is actually in front of you. You feel the finished thing finishing, and you let it finish. That is why people trust you with what is precious — you do not cling to it and you do not cut it early. You hold what is yours to hold and release what is yours to release, and the timing is good.

Right now the knowing is running ahead of the calendar. Endings are being declared before the thing has finished, so you are standing in a cleared field with nothing in it but the clearing. Being with one person where they actually are, without arranging anything, brings the timing back — it is not a detour from the work, it is the work at the speed of what is real.
cells.sheetLine: You are ending things ahead of their time and calling it care.

cells.tense: You stopped deciding what to keep, and you are still standing where you stopped — the field unread, the endings unspoken, everything held because nothing was sorted.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are genuinely drawn to and take one real step toward it today — not the safe one, the one you would choose if nobody were grading it.
cells.core:
When this is working, you know what matters before you can explain why, and you act on that knowing. The finished thing gets released without drama. What is alive stays and gets tended. Rooms you walk into get clearer because you were in them, and you never have to raise your voice to make that happen.

What has stopped is the sorting. Nothing is being released, nothing is being kept on purpose, so everything sits in the same unfinished pile and none of it grows. The way back is through what you are drawn to, not through what you think you are supposed to want. Let one real pull move you one step today and the knowing starts working again on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You still know what matters. You have just stopped choosing.

cells.tense: You are deciding what gets released and what gets kept all day long — and you talk about it as if the structure were doing the deciding, not you.
cells.ask: Say plainly, once, that one decision about what stays and what goes is yours — and let it stand without softening it.
cells.core:
When this is working, you set what holds and what moves on, and you do it in plain view. The room arranges itself around what you decided, not because you pushed but because you said a true thing clearly at the right moment. What is finished ends. What is alive is protected. People build on what you put down without asking who put it there.

That work is already happening. What is missing is the claim. Say that one call was yours, without hedging it, and the authority stops being something that happens around you and becomes something you carry.
